title: Motion: Chapter Introduction
subject: Physics
objective: Sitting still? With the Earth you are moving at about 1,500 km/h. Motion is a change of position with time, measured from a reference point, and this chapter gives the tools to describe it.

fill.q: Motion is a change of ____ with time.
Motion is always described relative to a ____ point.
On a distance-time graph, a flat line means the object is at ____.
A steeper distance-time graph means the object is moving ____.

tf.q: A chair is at rest for you but moving for an observer on the Sun.
tf.explain: Rest and motion depend on the reference point.

tf.q: Speed and velocity mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explain: Velocity also has a direction; speed does not.

tf.q: A distance-time graph can tell us whether an object is moving.
tf.explain: A changing distance shows motion; a flat line shows rest.

tf.q: Acceleration tells how fast an object is.
tf.explain: It tells how fast the velocity changes.

ar.r: The same object can be at rest for one observer and moving for another.
ar.explain: R is the meaning of relative motion.

ar.a: A flat distance-time graph shows uniform motion.
ar.r: On a flat graph the distance does not change with time.
ar.explain: A is false: flat means rest. R is true.

mcq.q: Which quantity describes how fast velocity changes?
mcq.explain: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

mcq.q: On a distance-time graph, which line shows the fastest motion?
mcq.explain: Steeper slope = more distance per second.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a tool of this chapter?
mcq.explain: Density belongs to matter, not motion.

short.q: Why do we need a reference point to describe motion?
short.solution: Position is measured from some point. The same object can be still for one observer and moving for another, so motion is meaningless without stating the reference.

short.q: Name the main quantities this chapter uses and what each tells us.
short.solution: Distance/displacement: how far and in which direction. Speed/velocity: how fast (velocity with direction). Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes. Graphs: show all these at a glance.

match.explain: These are the chapter's basic definitions.
